subject: DRF sDTF plot corresponding with mirt.info-plot?

messages.author: eab9582ba50c948a
messages.subject: DRF sDTF plot corresponding with mirt.info-plot?
parts:
Hey Phil,

I just discovered your DRF-function and are really loving it! :)

Is the scale of the sDTF measurement corresponding with the scale of the info-plot of the mirt model? Would it make sense to plot those two together in one diagram to see the sDTF-impact relativ to the information curve of the whole scale? If yes, how can I do so? Somehow with R lattice functions?

Thanks a lot for all your work and support!

Martin

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DRF sDTF plot corresponding with mirt.info-plot?
parts:
Hi Martin,

Glad you like the DRF family of statistics. I'm working more in this area again, and hopefully will have a paper or two come out on some recent developments and relationship with previous effect sizes in the IRT literature. 

Regarding your question, no the scale of the DRF plots is not in the scale of the information plots, only the x-axis containing theta would be the same. You could include the information function as a superimposed idea similar to how the g(theta) input is used to obtain the marginal effect sizes (sDRF, uDRF, etc), and indeed weighing by the inverse of the information function is something that has been proposed earlier in the literature, but this would require some customized plotting with some lower-level functions in mirt like testinfo() and probtrace() (I'd recommend using ggplot2 for this). HTH for now.

Phil
